bug_semantics: Apache MINA IoBuffer.getObject() deserializes with a custom ObjectInputStream. After the CVE-2024-52046 allowlist, AbstractIoBuffer.resolveClass() still had two branches: if ObjectStreamClass.forClass() was non-null it consulted acceptMatchers, but if forClass() was null (primitive/type-0 and other unresolved descriptors) it called Class.forName(name, false, classLoader) with no filter. An attacker who can supply serialized bytes to getObject() therefore bypasses the classname allowlist and can cause arbitrary class loading / gadget deserialization (CWE-502 RCE). The 2026 patch applies acceptMatchers before any Class.forName, on both branches.
flaw_origin: The two-branch resolveClass (null vs non-null forClass) dates to DIRMINA-990/991 commit c1792331521ec1f50e9c71228a20ca4ab21029fa (2014) with no allowlist on either path. The CVE-2024-52046 fix on 2.2.X, 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea (2024-11-04, subject 'pom.xml'), added acceptMatchers and attached the matcher loop only to the else branch, leaving the clazz==null Class.forName path unchanged. That incomplete pairing is this bypass. Immediate parent 23e6ee17bae46bb8e7a76dd7aeb508ec89e76a25 has the two-branch Class.forName but no acceptMatchers. Parallel incomplete ports: 834396355766e0c8f6bbf0493d4588b3fa9d347d (2.0.X, first in 2.0.27) and cdb59eb6131696a440870ab89ad0e20804eb5ca7 (2.1.X, first in 2.1.10).
